resources.string: Now: none chosen (Android asks each time)
The levels appear once Polylute is the home app.
Android has not confirmed the requested level.
This device is a Device Owner, so it stays Dedicated. To change level, stop being the device owner.
Polylute is your home screen. Nothing is locked: Android works as usual.
Android’s app pinning keeps Polylute on screen until you unpin it. No Device Owner, no adb, no reset.
To unpin: with gesture navigation swipe up and hold; with buttons hold Back and Overview. Android may ask for your PIN.
App pinning is off in Android. Turn it on in Settings, Security (it may be called “Pin windows”), then come back.
Dedicated locks Polylute with Android’s Lock Task and manages the lock screen. It needs Device Owner.
Requirements: no accounts or extra users on the device when you do it (a new or factory-reset phone, or remove every account first), USB debugging on, and a computer with adb.
Android may refuse (for example if an account exists). Nothing is active until Android confirms it.
Polylute is the home app and this device is a Device Owner, but Android is not holding the lock. “Return to DAP” locks it again.
Clears the lock, lock screen and home policies, then gives up Device Owner. No reset needed.

Polylute stops Lock Task, clears the allowlist, lock screen and home policies it set, and then gives up Device Owner. The phone goes back to Launcher or App Mode and needs no reset. To be dedicated again it must be provisioned again with adb.
Polylute is no longer the device owner.
Polylute is no longer the device owner. It is still the home app: change that with “Choose home app”.
Could not stop Lock Task. Device Owner was kept, and the policies and the lock were put back as they were and checked.
Could not clear every policy. Device Owner was kept, and the policies and the lock were put back as they were and checked.
Android still lists Polylute as the device owner. The policies and the lock were put back as they were and checked.

Could not confirm whether Polylute is still the device owner, so nothing else was applied and the lock was left off. Settings › System › Maintenance shows “Device Owner”: if it says Active, try again after choosing Polylute under “Choose home app”.
Could not check whether Polylute is the device owner. Nothing was changed. Try again.
Android still lists Polylute as the device owner, and the policies and the lock could not be confirmed back. Choose Polylute under “Choose home app” to contain it again.
Could not clear every policy, and the policies and the lock could not be confirmed back. Device Owner was kept. Choose Polylute under “Choose home app” to contain it again.
Could not stop Lock Task, and the policies and the lock could not be confirmed back. Device Owner was kept. Choose Polylute under “Choose home app” to contain it again.
Android still lists Polylute as the device owner. This device was not locked, so there was nothing to put back.
Could not clear every policy. Device Owner was kept. This device was not locked, so there was nothing to put back.
Could not stop Lock Task. Device Owner was kept. This device was not locked, so there was nothing to put back.
Polylute stops Lock Task and clears its home policy, then Android shows its home app picker. Pick another launcher; if you cancel, Polylute locks again.
